Package hadur2.core.shieldmode

Class ShieldMode

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.shieldmode.ShieldMode
public final class ShieldMode extends Object
Hadur's own bullet shield (SHIELD-5, SHIELD-6): sit still and shoot the enemy's bullets down.

Against a still target most guns fire head-on, so the heading of each enemy bullet can be worked out from where the two robots stood. For each enemy wave that would hit us, the mode plans a bullet, no stronger than the enemy's, that meets it in mid-air (ShieldGeometry), stepping 0.1 px sideways on the tick before it fires so the two paths are not collinear. Between shields it fires at the enemy only when its gun will be cool again in time for the enemy's next shot. The heading is predicted by twelve predictors: four head-on bases (from where the enemy stood on the tick before it fired, from its firing point, from where its velocity was taking it, and at where we stood on the firing tick), each plain, plus a learned offset, and plus a learned offset times our lateral direction. The predictor that has matched the most enemy bullets exactly is used.

When it is on (SHIELD-5). ShieldList is asked once, with the opponent's name at the first scan. For a listed opponent each round opens in shield mode. For anyone else, and when the list is empty, the mode never starts and every method here returns at once without a record: the duel plays exactly as it did before this class existed. Only the Duel's brain makes one, and only for a battle of one opponent.

When it is left.

  • For the rest of the battle (SHIELD-6): the enemy's bullet damage has exceeded the ShieldBudget's allowance, the amount that would hold our score share at 85%.
  • For the rest of the round, back on at the next round's start:
    • close: the enemy is within CLOSE_RANGE px, so a rammer is on us;
    • rammed: the enemy drove into us;
    • unpredicted: MAX_UNPREDICTED_HITS of its bullets hit us that no predictor had matched, so the predictions are failing;
    • outhit: at least MIN_HITS_TO_JUDGE of its bullets hit us and more than we shot down;
    • quiet: it has fired nothing for QUIET_TICKS ticks, so there is nothing to shield against and the gun is better used by the duel;
    • duress: the engine has skipped turns and the duel is in RES-14's duress.

Records, written only when the opponent is listed: SH,round,tick,on, SH,round,tick,exit,reason and SH,round,tick,off,budget as the mode changes, and at each round's end SR,round,tick,shieldShots,intercepts,hitsTaken,unpredicted, attackShots,damageTaken,allowed,exit.

Plain Java and the engine's physics only; deterministic (CORE-2, RES-6), and every list is bounded (RES-2).

    • onEnemyShot

      public void onEnemyShot(long fireTime, double power)
      An enemy bullet of power fired in the enemy's tick fireTime, from where it stood at that tick. Its heading is predicted four ways, all head-on at where we stood on the tick before: from where the enemy stood then (0), from its firing point (1), from where its velocity was taking it (2), and at where we stood on the firing tick (3).
      Parameters:
      fireTime - the tick the bullet left
      power - the bullet's power

    • ownBulletResolved

      public boolean ownBulletResolved(double power, double heading)
      Whether a bullet of ours that has just hit, missed or met a bullet is one this mode shot at an enemy bullet, and so no evidence about the enemy's aim (not SHIELD-1's detector's, not the hit rate's). A bullet is told by its power and its heading, the gun's heading on the tick it left, which the engine's event carries; an attack bullet of the same power left along another heading and is not taken for it. With no heading (NaN, from an older transcript) the oldest shield bullet of that power is taken. The shield bullet found is taken off the list.
      Parameters:
      power - the bullet's power
      heading - the bullet's absolute heading, radians, or NaN when unknown
      Returns:
      whether it was a shield bullet

    • tick

      public ShieldMode.Command tick(ShieldMode.Situation s)
      One tick of shield mode. Returns null when the tick's own check has just ended the mode for the round (close or quiet); the duel then plays the tick as it would without shield mode.
      Parameters:

      Returns:
      what to do, or null if the mode has been left
